title: Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026: Fully Remote Global Research Fellowship for Professionals Transitioning into AI Governance
summary: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping industries, governments, and societies worldwide. As AI systems become increasingly powerful, the need for skilled professionals capable of developing effective governance frameworks, safety policies, and risk mitigation strategies has never been greater. To help address this growing global challenge, Arcadia Impact has opened applications for its AI Governance Taskforce Autumn 2026 Cohort , a prestigious research programme designed for experienced professionals who want to transition into frontier AI governance. This highly selective programme offers participants an opportunity to conduct policy-relevant AI governance research alongside internationally recognized experts while maintaining their current professional commitments. Running over 12 weeks on a part-time basis, the programme is fully remote and welcomes applicants from around the world. Although voluntary and unpaid, the fellowship provides invaluable exposure, professional networking opportunities, practical research experience, and a proven pathway into careers focused on AI governance, AI safety, and policy development. About the Arcadia Impact AI Governance Taskforce The AI Governance Taskforce is a specialized research programme that supports experienced professionals seeking to transition into careers focused on reducing catastrophic and systemic risks associated with transformative artificial intelligence. Unlike many AI education programmes that focus on technical development or AI ethics generally, the AI Governance Taskforce specifically concentrates on frontier AI governance . Participants work on policy-focused research designed to improve governance systems capable of addressing advanced AI risks before they become major global threats. The programme enables professionals from diverse disciplines to apply their existing expertise to one of the world s fastest-growing policy areas while receiving mentorship from leaders in AI governance and safety. Why This Programme Matters As governments, international organizations, and technology companies race to regulate increasingly advanced AI systems, there is a significant global shortage of professionals who understand both public policy and frontier AI governance. Arcadia Impact created the AI Governance Taskforce to bridge this gap by providing professionals with: Practical research experience Exposure to real-world AI governance challenges High-level mentorship Collaborative policy development experience Professional networks within the AI safety community Participants leave the programme with stronger credentials that position them for future opportunities in AI governance, research, public policy, and international organizations. Programme Overview The Autumn 2026 cohort has been carefully structured to accommodate working professionals. Programme Details Programme Duration: 12 weeks Programme Dates: 12 October 2026 – 15 January 2027 Year-End Break: Two-week holiday break between 18 December 2026 and 4 January 2027 Commitment: Approximately 8 hours per week Delivery Mode: Fully remote Location: Global Programme Type: Voluntary and unpaid Available Positions: Approximately 20 Research Associate places Participants can continue with their existing careers while contributing to meaningful AI governance research. What Participants Will Do Research Associates become members of multidisciplinary research teams composed of four individuals. Each team works closely with: A dedicated Research Team Leader A leading AI governance expert Other experienced professionals from diverse disciplines Together, they investigate pressing AI governance questions and produce policy-oriented research intended to influence real-world decision-making. Typical research outputs include: Academic-style preprint papers Policy briefs Government policy memoranda Research articles Stakeholder reports These publications are designed to address challenges surrounding advanced AI governance and catastrophic AI risks. Learn from World-Leading AI Governance Experts Participants receive direct guidance from senior practitioners working across some of the world s most respected AI safety and governance organizations. Expert partners have included professionals affiliated with: UK AI Security Institute (AISI) Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI) AI Incident Database (AIID) MIT AI Risk Initiative (AIRI) Centre for Long-Term Resilience (CLTR) SaferAI The Future Society Future of Life Institute (FLI) Leading universities and academic institutions Research Team Leaders work alongside these experts to ensure projects remain academically rigorous and policy relevant. Areas of Research Projects typically focus on governance challenges surrounding frontier AI systems. Examples include: AI incident monitoring AI governance frameworks AI safety cases International AI policy Frontier AI regulation AI risk management Open-source intelligence for AI governance Dangerous capability thresholds AI accountability mechanisms Loss-of-control scenarios International governance infrastructure Research themes evolve with emerging developments in AI governance. Outstanding Career Outcomes for Alumni One of the strongest features of the AI Governance Taskforce is its exceptional alumni network. Graduates have progressed into positions at organizations including: Google DeepMind SaferAI ControlAI Pour Demain Oxford Martin AI Governance Initiative MIT AI Risk Initiative Centre for Long-Term Resilience The Future Society GovAI IAPS Future Impact Group Many alumni have also: Secured research management positions Joined international AI governance fellowships Collaborated with renowned AI researcher Yoshua Bengio Started independent AI governance initiatives Returned to the Taskforce as Research Team Leaders These achievements demonstrate the programme s effectiveness as a launchpad for careers in frontier AI governance. International Recognition of Research Research produced through the Taskforce has received significant international recognition. Achievements include: Acceptance at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML) Technical AI Governance Workshop Best Paper Award recognition Co-authorship opportunities with expert partners Features in Time Magazine Coverage in the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists Publication in the AI Policy Bulletin These accomplishments reflect the quality and impact of the programme s research outputs. Who Should Apply? Arcadia Impact is seeking motivated professionals who have already begun transitioning toward careers in frontier AI governance. Applicants should demonstrate genuine commitment rather than simply exploring the field. Professionals from a wide variety of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including: Law Public Policy Economics Political Science International Relations Engineering Machine Learning Software Engineering Systems Engineering Mechanical Engineering Safety Engineering Computer Science Philosophy Social Sciences Humanities Management Applicants do not need to possess deep technical AI expertise. Eligibility Requirements Applicants should be able to: Commit approximately eight hours per week throughout the programme. Work effectively within a structured remote research team. Demonstrate commitment to reducing catastrophic risks from frontier AI. Show evidence of progressing toward a career in AI governance. Communicate clearly through writing and research. Exercise sound judgement when evaluating AI governance challenges. Work independently with minimal supervision. Arcadia Impact encourages applications even from candidates who meet only part of the preferred profile. What the Selection Committee Looks For Applications are assessed using several criteria, including: 1. Application Process The Autumn 2026 selection process consists of four stages. title: Free Net Zero Learning Pathway by UN SDG:Learn | Learn Climate Action and Science-Based Targets
summary: Are you interested in climate action, sustainability, and achieving a net-zero future? The UN SDG:Learn Net Zero Learning Pathway offers a free opportunity for learners worldwide to develop a comprehensive understanding of net-zero emissions, climate science, and science-based targets. Developed through collaboration with leading United Nations partners, this self-paced learning pathway helps individuals, professionals, students, policymakers, and organizations understand how to align climate actions with global goals and contribute to a more sustainable future. The pathway combines three specialized courses that guide learners from foundational concepts to practical implementation of net-zero strategies. About the Net Zero Learning Pathway The Net Zero Learning Pathway introduces participants to the science behind climate change, the importance of achieving net-zero emissions, and the frameworks used by organizations worldwide to set and achieve climate goals. Through a structured learning journey, participants will: • Understand the fundamentals of net-zero emissions. • Learn why climate action is critical for sustainable development. • Explore practical approaches to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. • Understand science-based target methodologies. • Learn how organizations align climate commitments with the 1.5°C pathway. • Gain knowledge of internationally recognized net-zero standards. The pathway is completely online and self-paced, allowing learners to study at their convenience. What You Will Learn The learning pathway is divided into three modules that progressively build climate knowledge and practical skills. Module 1 : Understanding Net Zero Course 1 : The Net-Zero Standard Provider : United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) This course introduces learners to the concept of net-zero emissions and explains why reaching net zero is essential for addressing climate change. Participants will explore: • Climate science fundamentals. • The role of net-zero strategies in limiting global warming. • Key concepts and terminology related to net-zero commitments. • Practical actions that organizations and individuals can take to reduce emissions. This course provides the foundation needed to understand broader climate action frameworks. Module 2 : Science-Based Targets for Net Zero Course 2 : Net Zero 101: What, Why and How Provider :United Nations University (UNU) This introductory course examines the importance of net-zero commitments and provides practical guidance on how organizations can contribute to global climate goals. Participants will learn: • What net zero means in practice. • Why net-zero commitments matter. • How emissions reductions contribute to climate mitigation. • Key approaches for implementing climate strategies. • The relationship between sustainability and long-term resilience. The course is ideal for individuals seeking a broader understanding of climate solutions and net-zero implementation. Module 3: The Net-Zero Standard in Practice Course 3 : Setting Science-Based Targets to Achieve Net-Zero Provider : United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) This advanced course focuses on helping organizations establish science-based targets that align with global climate objectives. Participants will explore: • Science-based target methodologies. • Setting near-term and long-term emissions reduction goals. • Aligning organizational targets with the 1.5°C climate pathway. • Best practices for implementing the Net-Zero Standard. • Strategies for measuring and tracking climate progress. This course is particularly valuable for sustainability professionals, business leaders, policymakers, and organizations seeking to strengthen their climate commitments. Who Should Enroll? The Net Zero Learning Pathway is suitable for: • Students and young professionals. • Climate and sustainability advocates. • Environmental practitioners. • Corporate sustainability teams. • Government officials and policymakers. • NGO professionals. • Researchers and academics. • Anyone interested in climate action and sustainable development. No prior experience is required to begin the pathway. Benefits of the Learning Pathway Participants will benefit from: • Free access to high-quality United Nations learning resources. • Flexible self-paced learning. • Expert insights from leading global institutions. • Practical knowledge on climate action and net-zero implementation. • Skills relevant to sustainability and environmental careers. • Increased understanding of science-based climate targets. • Enhanced capacity to contribute to organizational and community climate initiatives. Why Net Zero Matters Net-zero emissions have become a central goal in global efforts to combat climate change. Governments, businesses, institutions, and communities worldwide are adopting net-zero commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming. Understanding how net-zero frameworks operate and how science-based targets are established is increasingly important for professionals working in sustainability, environmental management, policy development, and corporate responsibility. This learning pathway provides a valuable opportunity to gain these critical skills at no cost. Conclusion The UN SDG:Learn Net Zero Learning Pathway offers a comprehensive and accessible introduction to climate action, net-zero standards, and science-based targets. Through three expertly designed courses from the United Nations Global Compact and United Nations University , learners can build the knowledge and practical skills needed to support a sustainable, low-carbon future. Whether you are a student, sustainability professional, policymaker, or simply passionate about climate action, this free learning opportunity can help you better understand the pathways toward achieving global climate goals and creating meaningful environmental impact.
